justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a modest upward drift across horizons, starting near 315.5 for the one-day forecast and rising gradually to 320 at one month. The one-day estimate was anchored primarily by recent price action and short-term momentum, assuming no major macro surprises overnight. The slight upward bias in the weekly and monthly estimates reflects a baseline assumption of continued but modest positive drift, consistent with longer-run trend behavior in many financial assets. I did not assume any strong directional catalyst, so the progression is gentle rather than aggressive.

The confidence interval widths expand significantly as the horizon lengthens, which reflects the well-established principle that uncertainty compounds over time. At one day, the 90% interval spans roughly 17 points, capturing typical intraday and overnight volatility. By one week, the interval widens to 34 points, incorporating the possibility of several days of compounding moves or a sudden shift in sentiment. At one month, the 70-point interval reflects the reality that over four weeks, macro data releases, central bank communications, earnings, and geopolitical developments could collectively push the price meaningfully in either direction. Volatility regime uncertainty also contributed to the wider bands at longer horizons, since it is difficult to know whether current conditions will persist.

Several specific risks could push outcomes outside even the stated intervals. On the upside, a surprise dovish policy shift from a major central bank, a significant positive economic data print, or a risk-on sentiment surge driven by geopolitical resolution could propel prices well above the upper bounds. On the downside, an unexpected hawkish policy surprise, a financial stress event such as a credit market dislocation, or a sharp deterioration in global growth expectations could push prices below the lower bounds. Liquidity conditions also matter — if market depth thins for any reason, moves can overshoot fundamentally justified levels by a meaningful margin, making even wide intervals look narrow in retrospect.
